easy.def: A big container for washing or holding things.
examples: I took a bath in the tub.
The tub is full.
The tub is white.

more.def: A large, open container used for washing or holding things, or a bathtub.
examples: The baby splashed in the tub.
We filled the tub with warm water.
The kids kept their toys in a plastic tub.

easy.def: A very big, low brass music tool.
examples: He plays the tuba.
The tuba is loud.
A tuba was in the band.

more.def: A very large brass musical instrument that plays deep, low notes.
examples: The tuba player marched at the back of the band.
The tuba's deep notes rumbled through the hall.
She learned to play the tuba in the school band.

easy.def: A long, hollow pipe or case.
examples: I squeezed the tube of paste.
Water flows through a tube.
A straw is a small tube.

more.def: A long, hollow pipe, or a soft case with a cap that holds something to squeeze out.
examples: A tube carried water from the tank to the sink.
He squeezed paint out of the tube.
A drinking straw is a thin tube.

easy.def: To push the edge of something in neatly.
examples: Tuck in your shirt.
Mom tucked the blanket around me.
She tucked the napkin.

more.def: To push or fold the edges of something in so that it is neat or snug.
examples: He tucked the corners of the sheet under the mattress.
He tucked his shirt into his pants.
The bird tucked its head under its wing.

easy.def: The day after Monday.
examples: Tuesday is pizza day at school.
I have a swimming lesson on Tuesday.
Mom is home on Tuesday.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Monday and before Wednesday.
examples: The recycling truck comes on Tuesday morning.
Our book club meets every Tuesday after school.
On Tuesday, the first snow of the year fell.

easy.def: To pull something hard.
examples: I tug on the rope.
The dog tugged my sleeve.
She tugged the door.

more.def: To pull something hard and quickly.
examples: I tugged on the rope.
The puppy tugged at my sleeve.
She tugged at the stuck door until it opened.

easy.def: A hard, quick pull.
examples: I felt a tug on my hat.
The dog gave a tug.
He gave the rope a tug.

more.def: A hard, quick pull.
examples: I felt a tug on my sleeve.
The fish gave a tug on the line.
With one tug, the door came open.

easy.def: Money you pay for school.
examples: Tuition is paid each year.
The school charges tuition.
Dad paid the tuition.

more.def: The money that is paid for teaching, especially at a school or college.
examples: The college charges a lot of tuition each year.
Dad paid my music tuition each month.
Some private schools charge tuition, but public schools do not.

easy.def: To fall down and roll over.
examples: I tumbled down the hill.
The blocks tumbled to the floor.
The puppy tumbled over.

more.def: To fall or roll over suddenly, often in a loose and clumsy way.
examples: The puppy tumbled down the steps and then bounced up again.
The tower of blocks tumbled over when I touched it.
Boxes tumbled from the shelf and scattered across the floor.

easy.def: A fall.
examples: I took a tumble in the grass.
He had a tumble off his bike.
The tumble made us laugh.

more.def: A sudden fall or roll, often a harmless one.
examples: She took a tumble in the soft snow and came up laughing.
The kitten took a tumble off the sofa but landed on its feet.
The gymnast did a quick tumble across the mat.

easy.def: A word for stomach or belly.
examples: My tummy hurts.
I rubbed my tummy.
The baby has a round tummy.

more.def: A child's word for the stomach or belly.
examples: My tummy hurts because I ate too fast.
The baby giggled when I tickled her tummy.
I rubbed my tummy after the big dinner.

easy.def: A large sea fish that people eat.
examples: I eat tuna.
A tuna swam.
We had a tuna sandwich.

more.def: A large fish that lives in the sea and is eaten as food, often from a can.
examples: I made a tuna sandwich for lunch.
A tuna swam past the boat.
Tuna can swim very fast.

easy.def: A song or a set of notes that you can hum.
examples: I hummed a happy tune.
She plays a tune on the flute.
The tune stuck in my head.

more.def: A group of musical notes that makes a pleasing song.
examples: The band played a lively tune.
I could not get the tune out of my head.
She whistled a tune as she walked.

easy.def: A long, loose shirt.
examples: The knight wore a tunic.
The tunic is long.
She wore a blue tunic.

more.def: A long, loose piece of clothing that reaches to the knees, worn long ago.
examples: The knight wore a tunic over his armor.
The boy's tunic was belted at the waist.
The Roman soldier wore a tunic.

easy.def: A long path under the ground or through a hill.
examples: The train goes through the tunnel.
We dug a tunnel in the sand.
The tunnel is dark.

more.def: A long passage dug under the ground or through a mountain or hill.
examples: The train rushed through a tunnel in the mountain.
Moles dig tunnels under the garden.
Cars went through the tunnel under the river.

easy.def: A long cloth wrapped around the head.
examples: He wore a turban on his head.
The turban was blue.
A turban is made of cloth.

more.def: A head covering made of a long piece of cloth wound around the head.
examples: The man wore a bright orange turban.
Turbans have been worn in many parts of the world for hundreds of years.
The traveler wrapped a turban around his head against the sun.

easy.def: A big wheel that spins to make power.
examples: The wind turbine spins.
A turbine makes power.
We saw a tall turbine.

more.def: A machine with blades that are turned by wind, water or steam to make electricity.
examples: The wind turbine's huge blades turned slowly in the breeze to make electricity.
Water flowing through the dam spins a turbine.
A line of turbines stood along the hilltop.

easy.def: Grass and the soil under it.
examples: The turf was soft.
We played on turf.
The workers laid turf.

more.def: A top layer of soil with grass growing in it, or a grassy playing field.
examples: The groundskeeper rolled out fresh turf for the new field.
The players slid across the soft, wet turf.
We kicked the soccer ball across the green turf.

easy.def: A big bird that people eat at Thanksgiving.
examples: We ate turkey on Thanksgiving.
A wild turkey ran across the road.
The turkey is big.

more.def: A large bird with a bare head and a fan-shaped tail, raised for food or found wild.
examples: Many families eat roast turkey on Thanksgiving.
A wild turkey fanned its tail feathers to impress the others.
Turkeys can run fast and can fly for short distances.

easy.def: To go around or face a new way.
examples: Turn left here.
The wheel turns.
She turned around.

more.def: To move around a point, or to change direction.
examples: The wheels of the bus turn slowly on the icy road.
Turn left at the corner to get to the library.
He turned his head when someone called his name.

easy.def: To become something new.
examples: Leaves turn red.
Ice turns into water.
The sky turned dark.

more.def: To change into something different.
examples: Caterpillars turn into butterflies.
The leaves turn orange and gold in the fall.
The milk turned sour after sitting out all day.

easy.def: Your time to do something in a game.
examples: It is my turn.
Now it is your turn.
She waits for her turn.

more.def: The time when it is your chance to do something, one after another.
examples: Everyone gets a turn on the swing.
It is your turn to roll the dice.
We took turns reading the story aloud.

easy.def: A round white vegetable that grows in the ground.
examples: I ate a turnip.
The turnip is white.
We grew turnips.

more.def: A round white vegetable with a purple top that grows under the ground and is eaten cooked.
examples: Grandpa pulled a big turnip out of the ground.
We cooked turnips and carrots in the soup.
A turnip has a mild, slightly sharp taste.

easy.def: A pastry folded over a filling.
examples: I ate an apple turnover.
The turnover is sweet.
She ate a turnover.

more.def: A small pastry made by folding dough over a filling.
examples: I ate an apple turnover for dessert.
The baker made cherry turnovers.
She put jam inside the turnover.

easy.def: A big road where you pay to drive.
examples: We drove on the turnpike.
The turnpike is fast.
The turnpike has tolls.

more.def: A wide highway that people pay to use.
examples: We paid a toll to drive on the turnpike.
The turnpike was crowded on Friday.
Cars zipped along the turnpike.

easy.def: A blue-green color.
examples: The sea is turquoise.
My shirt is turquoise.
I like turquoise.

more.def: A bright blue-green color, or a stone of that color.
examples: The sea was a clear turquoise.
She painted the door turquoise.
The ring had a turquoise stone.

easy.def: Blue-green.
examples: A turquoise shirt.
The turquoise water was warm.
The turquoise bird flew.

more.def: Having a bright blue-green color.
examples: The turquoise water was warm and clear.
She wore a turquoise necklace.
A turquoise parrot sat in the tree.

easy.def: A small tower on the corner of a building.
examples: The castle has a turret.
A flag is on the turret.
A girl looked out of the turret.

more.def: A small tower that sticks out from the top or corner of a building, such as a castle.
examples: The castle has a tall turret on each corner.
A flag flew from the top of the turret.
The girl looked out of the turret window at the hills.

easy.def: An animal with a hard shell on its back.
examples: The turtle is slow.
A turtle hid in its shell.
The turtle crossed the road.

more.def: A slow, hard-shelled animal that lives in water or on land and can pull its head into its shell.
examples: The turtle pulled its head into its shell.
Sea turtles swim long distances.
A turtle slowly crossed the road.

easy.def: A shirt with a high, close collar.
examples: I wore a turtleneck.
The turtleneck is warm.
I saw a red turtleneck.

more.def: A shirt or sweater with a high, close collar that folds over at the neck.
examples: I wore a warm turtleneck to school.
The turtleneck kept her neck warm in the snow.
Dad pulled on a gray turtleneck.

easy.def: A teacher who helps one student.
examples: My tutor helps me with math.
The tutor is kind.
I have a tutor.

more.def: A person who teaches one student or a small group, to give extra help.
examples: My tutor helps me with reading after school.
A math tutor visited every Tuesday.
The tutor explained the hard problem again.

easy.def: Extra help with schoolwork from a person.
examples: I get tutoring in math.
Tutoring helped me.
She does tutoring.

more.def: Extra teaching that someone gives you one-on-one or in a small group to help you learn.
examples: I get tutoring in math after school to help me catch up.
Tutoring helped her improve her reading.
He does tutoring for younger students on Saturday.

easy.def: A short, puffy skirt that ballet dancers wear.
examples: The dancer wore a tutu.
My tutu is pink.
She twirled in her tutu.

more.def: A short, stiff, puffy skirt worn by ballet dancers.
examples: The little dancer wore a pink tutu.
Her tutu spread out as she twirled.
I put on my tutu for the dance show.

easy.def: A formal suit that a man wears to a fancy event.
examples: He wore a tuxedo.
The tuxedo is black.
Dad rented a tuxedo.

more.def: A formal black suit with a bow tie, worn to fancy parties and weddings.
examples: He wore a black tuxedo to the wedding.
Dad rented a tuxedo for the party.
The waiter wore a white shirt and a tuxedo jacket.
